worked_examples.problem: In-Text Question & Exercise (Section 8.1, 8.2 & p. 6): (a) A Mendelian cross between tall pea plants (TT) and short pea plants (tt) produced all tall plants in the F1 generation. When F1 plants were self-pollinated, what was the ratio of tall to short plants in the F2 generation? (b) How is the sex of a human child determined genetically?
worked_examples.given: Mendelian monohybrid cross; Human chromosomal sex determination.
worked_examples.formula: Monohybrid phenotypic ratio 3 : 1, genotypic ratio 1 : 2 : 1. Sex determination: Female XX, Male XY. Probability of male vs female = 50% each.
worked_examples.substitution: Punnett square analysis: F1 (Tt) x F1 (Tt) -> TT, Tt, Tt, tt.
worked_examples.calculation:
(a) Mendelian Monohybrid Cross:
1. Parents: TT (pure tall) x tt (pure dwarf).
2. Gametes: T and t -> F1 Generation: All Tt (heterozygous tall; 'T' is dominant over recessive 't').
3. Selfing F1 (Tt x Tt):
   Gametes: T, t from both parents.
   F2 Genotypes: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt (Genotypic ratio 1 : 2 : 1).
   F2 Phenotypes: 3 Tall : 1 Short (Phenotypic ratio 3 : 1, i.e. 75% tall, 25% dwarf).
(b) Sex Determination in Humans:
Human females have two homologous X chromosomes (XX), producing only one type of ovum carrying an X chromosome. Human males have heteromorphic sex chromosomes (XY), producing two types of sperm: 50% carry an X chromosome, and 50% carry a Y chromosome.
- If an X-sperm fertilises the ovum: Zygote is XX -> Female child.
- If a Y-sperm fertilises the ovum: Zygote is XY -> Male child.
Since fertilization by X or Y sperm is an equal random probability (50%), the child's genetic sex is determined strictly by the father's fertilising sperm.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: (a) F2 phenotypic ratio is 3 Tall : 1 Short (75% tall, 25% short); (b) Sex is determined by the sperm: X-sperm produces a girl (XX), Y-sperm produces a boy (XY) with 50% probability.
